en: The Questions of Milinda;
The Questions of the Puzzles;
The Chapter on the Indivisible.
7. The Question on the Sustaining of the Saṅgha of Bhikkhus “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata: “I shall sustain the saṅgha of bhikkhus,” or “The saṅgha of bhikkhus has me as its guide.”’”
Furthermore, when the Blessed One was illustrating the natural qualities of the Blessed One Metteyya, he spoke thus:
"He will lead a community of monks numbering many thousands, just as I now lead a community of monks numbering many hundreds.
If, venerable Nāgasena, it was said by the Blessed One—
“Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata: ‘I shall lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,’ or ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus has me as its guide.
Therefore, the statement that he leads a Saṅgha of many hundreds of bhikkhus is false.”
If it has been said by the Tathāgata:
"He will lead a community of many thousands of bhikkhus, just as I now lead a community of many hundreds of bhikkhus," then indeed, Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata: "I..."
“‘I shall lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,’ or ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is under my guidance’—that statement too is false;
this too is a dilemma from both sides that has come upon you, and it must be resolved by you.
“It was indeed spoken thus, Great King, by the Blessed One: ‘Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata: “I shall lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,” or “The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is under my guidance.”’”
Furthermore, O Great King, when the Blessed One was elucidating the natural qualities of the Blessed One Metteyya, he said:
“He will lead a community of monks numbering many thousands, just as I now lead a community of monks numbering many hundreds.
In this question, O Great King, one point is incomplete, while another point is complete.
“Great king, the Tathāgata does not follow after the assembly; rather, the assembly follows after the Tathāgata.
Great king, this notion of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ is merely conventional; it is not the ultimate truth. Great king, the Tathāgata’s affection has departed, his endearment has vanished.
The Tathāgata has no grasping even for the thought ‘mine’; yet, having taken up [the body], he remains as a refuge.”

"Just as, great king, the earth is the foundation and the shelter for beings dwelling upon it, and these beings dwell upon the earth, yet the great earth has no concern for them, thinking, 'These are mine';
even so, great king, the Tathāgata is the foundation and the shelter for all beings, and these beings dwell in the Tathāgata, yet the Tathāgata has no concern for them, thinking, 'These are mine.
Or again, great king, just as a vast great cloud, when raining down, provides growth for grasses, trees, domestic animals, and humans, and maintains their continuity."
All these beings depend upon the Teacher for their livelihood, yet the great cloud has no expectation of them, thinking, "These are mine.

In the same way, Great King, the Tathāgata generates and protects the wholesome qualities of all beings; all these beings depend upon the Teacher for their livelihood, yet the Tathāgata has no expectation of them, thinking, "These are mine.
For what reason?
“Because of the abandoning of the view of self,” [he said].
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! This question has been well-unraveled through many reasons;

what was deep has been made shallow, the knot has been untied, the thicket has been made non-thicketed, darkness has been turned into light, and the arguments of opponents have been shattered for the sons of the Conqueror.”
“The eye has arisen.
This is the seventh question on maintaining the community of bhikkhus.
